messages:
alex: Quick thought — ambiguous match case we saw yesterday: host=*.api.example.com vs header anchor x-service=payments. When both match, runtime picks host-first and we lose header preference. Can we run a small experiment to flip to header-first for 2% of traffic and measure fallout?

maya: +1 for an experiment. Curious how we'll score regressions though — latency? misrouted traffic metrics?

sam: Agree. We should track: 1) 5xxs where service != expected, 2) route-reason logs, 3) latency p50/p95. Also add a metric for 'selector-mismatch' count.

alex: Good call. Proposal: rollout key `matcher.fallback_policy=header_first` with override percent, and emit `match.reason` in trace for each request. Minimal config: 
```yaml
routes:
  - name: payments-host
    host: "*.api.example.com"
    service: payments-v1
  - name: payments-header
    headers:
      x-service: payments
    service: payments-candidate
```
Then enable header-first in 2% of prod.

ashley: Small UX note — Console should surface which policy is active per route and show a sparklines for selector-mismatch. Otherwise SRE will be confused when only 2% behave differently.

maya: Also we need a deterministic tie-breaker for equal-weight anchors (host vs header) so tests are reproducible. For experiment use sticky hashing on `request_id` so same client always sees same policy.

sam: If we change precedence, can we automatically fallback to host-first on capacity errors? i.e., header-first but if payments-candidate is at capacity, route to payments-v1. That preserves reliability.

alex: Yes — add policy chain: header_first -> if target_unavailable -> host_fallback. We'll log fallback events as `match.fallback_to_host` with downstream reason.

deploy-bot: rollout started: matcher.fallback_policy=header_first at 2% across prod (canary id: cf-1723).

ashley: Thx. I'll add a small Console card: policy, percent, fallback counts, selector-mismatch. Ping me when telemetry is wired and I'll prototype the card. :sparkles: 

maya: I'll own the eval. Will post a short runbook: what to rollback on (error spike > 3x, misroute rate > 0.1%).

alex: Great. I'll open a tiny PR for the flag + trace tags and add test vectors for host/header collision cases.

sam: One more: add a debug endpoint to query which rule would match given headers+host so we can reproduce in support. Very useful.

alex: Yep. `GET /_match-debug?host=...&x-service=...` — returns chosen-route and reason. Thanks team.
